markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. House of Representatives adjourns from substantive floor business for its pre-election 2026 recess after Issuance and before Sep 26, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from the U.S. House of Representatives qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The qualifying report must identify that the House has left substantive floor business for its pre-election recess. A daily adjournment, district work period, or pro forma session is insufficient unless the House reports that the pre-election recess has begun.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the candidate drops out.
markets.rules_primary: If Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. drops out of the 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate race before Sep 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
“Dropped out” means any of the following:
the candidate announces they are ending, suspending, or withdrawing from their campaign
the candidate files official withdrawal paperwork with relevant election authorities
the candidate publicly states they are no longer seeking the office
the candidate endorses another candidate while stating they are no longer running
the candidate is disqualified by election authorities or courts and does not appeal

The following do NOT constitute dropping out:
Losing a primary or election
Failing to qualify for debates or ballots
Temporarily suspending campaign activities without withdrawing
Being eliminated through the normal election process
Reducing campaign activities while remaining a candidate

Key provisions:
Once someone drops out per above criteria, the market resolves YES even if they later re-enter
“Suspending” a campaign is treated as dropping out unless the candidate explicitly states they remain a candidate
Withdrawing from the race counts even if the person remains on the ballot

Each market in this event resolves independently. A candidate not named in this event dropping out does not resolve any market here.
markets.subtitle: :: Alaska U.S. Senate race
markets.title: Will Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. drop out of the Alaska U.S. Senate race before Sep 1, 2026?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if  definitively calls the 2026 U.S. Senate majority.
markets.rules_primary: If the Associated Press makes its first definitive call of a winner for the 2026 U.S. Senate majority before 12AM ET on Nov 19, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The call must be an explicit declaration that a candidate, party, or option has won, will win, is projected to win, or equivalent clear language indicating the outlet has determined the winner. The call must appear on one of the outlet's primary platforms (main website, television broadcast, or official social media if that is their primary medium) and not be prefaced with qualifiers suggesting uncertainty such as "appears to," "likely to," "probably," or "may have." The relevant time is when the call first becomes publicly visible on the outlet's platform, not when it may have been written, decided internally, or prepared for publication. If the call is later retracted, the market nonetheless resolves to Yes based on the initial call time. Preliminary exit polls, reporting of other outlets' calls, conditional statements, opinion pieces, and technical glitches do not qualify as definitive calls.
markets.title: Will AP call the 2026 U.S. Senate majority before 12AM ET on Nov 19, 2026?

markets.rules_primary: If the number of Democratic U.S. House members elected from the 235 districts that Donald Trump carried in 2024 is at least 46 at the November 3, 2026 general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The qualifying districts are the 235 in which Trump received more votes than Harris in 2024, as calculated by The Downballot in its 2024 presidential results by congressional district table, for the district boundaries in use at the 2026 elections. That list is fixed as of Issuance and identified by state and district number, so later boundary changes and revisions to the 2024 vote totals do NOT add or remove districts.

A district counts only if the candidate elected there is the nominee of the Democratic Party. If a runoff is required to determine the winner of any race, the runoff result governs. Preliminary exit polls, reporting of other outlets' calls, conditional statements, opinion pieces, and technical glitches do not qualify as definitive calls.

markets.rules_primary: If WI-03 has the smallest margin of victory among all elections in the November 3, 2026 U.S. House general elections as of Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Margin of victory is calculated as the absolute percentage point difference between first and second place finishers. For two-candidate races, this is winner's percentage minus runner-up's percentage. For multi-candidate races, only the gap between first and second counts. For ranked choice/instant runoff elections, the margin from the final round is used.

Every U.S. House general election held November 3, 2026 is compared, not only the districts listed here, so if the smallest margin is in an unlisted district every market in this event resolves NO. Special elections to fill a vacancy do NOT count.

Votes for a candidate listed on more than one party line are combined.

If official results aren't available by the deadline but at least 95% of expected vote is counted, preliminary results are used. In case of identical margins (tied to the hundredth of a percentage point), tied options split the payout equally. Postponed elections or those without sufficient results by the deadline resolve to No.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the candidate drops out.
markets.rules_primary: If Max Miller drops out of the OH-07 race before Sep 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
“Dropped out” means any of the following:
Max Miller announces they are ending, suspending, or withdrawing from their campaign
Max Miller files official withdrawal paperwork with relevant election authorities
Max Miller publicly states they are no longer seeking the office
Max Miller endorses another candidate while stating they are no longer running
Max Miller is disqualified by election authorities or courts and does not appeal

The following do NOT constitute dropping out:
Losing a primary or election
Failing to qualify for debates or ballots
Temporarily suspending campaign activities without withdrawing
Being eliminated through the normal election process
Reducing campaign activities while remaining a candidate

Key provisions:
Once someone drops out per above criteria, the market resolves YES even if they later re-enter
“Suspending” a campaign is treated as dropping out unless Max Miller explicitly states they remain a candidate
For primary races, dropping out of the presidential race entirely counts as dropping out of that party’s primary
Withdrawing from the race counts even if the person remains on the ballot
markets.title: Will Max Miller drop out of the the OH-07 race before Sep 1, 2026?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if all elections have been decided and margins calculated.
markets.rules_primary: If Idaho has the smallest margin of victory among all elections in the 2026 United States Senate elections as of Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Margin of victory is calculated as the absolute percentage point difference between first and second place finishers. For two-candidate races, this is winner's percentage minus runner-up's percentage. For multi-candidate races, only the gap between first and second counts. For ranked choice/instant runoff elections, the margin from the final round is used.

If official results aren't available by the deadline but at least 95% of expected vote is counted, preliminary results are used. In case of identical margins (tied to the hundredth of a percentage point), tied options split the payout equally. Postponed elections or those without sufficient results by the deadline resolve to No.
markets.title: Will Idaho have the smallest margin of victory in 2026 United States Senate elections?

Except as otherwise specified, previously aired content, archival footage, and recordings captured at times, places, or events wholly separate from the featured address will not count.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of U.S. states that formally adopt a binding state-level moratorium on data-center development is at least 5 in 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A state qualifies upon final adoption of a binding law, executive order, regulation, or agency order that expressly targets data centers and prohibits or suspends a material governmental approval, permitting, interconnection, construction, expansion, or operation pathway for new or expanded data centers.

The measure may apply only to a defined class of data centers, including facilities above a specified power, water-use, computing-capacity, or size threshold, and may grandfather existing facilities or applications. It need not use the word “moratorium,” and a permanent prohibition also qualifies.

A qualifying state remains counted if the measure subsequently expires, is repealed, rescinded, superseded, or enjoined, provided it became legally operative. Local measures, project-specific holds, pending legislation, studies, reporting requirements, tax-incentive changes, and regulatory requirements that do not suspend development do not qualify.

Count as of July 21, 2026: 1 — New York. New York Executive Order 62, issued July 14, directs the Department of Environmental Conservation to hold certain incomplete discretionary-permit applications for the construction or expansion of data centers in abeyance. The order covers data centers consuming or capable of consuming at least 50 megawatts, and official state and NCSL materials identify it as the nation’s first statewide data-center moratorium.
markets.title: Will the number of U.S. states that formally adopt a binding state-level moratorium on data-center development be at least 5 in 2026?

markets.rules_primary: If the number of the 12 fiscal year 2027 regular appropriations bills that have become law is at least 5 before October 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Each of the 12 regular appropriations categories is counted separately. 

A standalone appropriations law counts as one, while an omnibus or minibus counts once for each regular appropriations bill enacted within it; for example, a package containing four regular appropriations divisions counts as four. 

Continuing resolutions, supplemental appropriations, and other funding measures do not count unless they enact one or more of the 12 regular appropriations bills. A regular appropriations bill counts regardless of its legislative vehicle, bill number, or whether it is enacted as a division of a broader law.

For example, in FY2019 the applicable number is 5: two minibuses covering Energy-Water, Legislative Branch, Military Construction–VA, Defense, and Labor-HHS-Education were enacted before October 1.

markets.rules_primary: If the regularly scheduled biennial federal general election for the U.S. House of Representatives is conducted on time in all 50 U.S. states on the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An election is "conducted on time" in a state if, on the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026, election officials in that state lawfully accept ballots cast by voters in such election in each of the state's U.S. House of Representatives congressional districts, such that votes cast on that date in each such district are eligible to be counted toward determining the winner of the election in that district. Lawful means of accepting ballots include in person at polling places, by mail, by absentee voting, by provisional ballot, or by other lawful means accepted on that date.

Localized disruptions within a congressional district do not disqualify that district from being "conducted on time" so long as ballots are lawfully accepted somewhere within the district on the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026. These include, without limitation:
Individual polling places opening late or closing early
Individual voting machines malfunctioning
Localized power, weather, or connectivity outages

However, if on the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026 no ballots are lawfully accepted anywhere within one or more of a state's congressional districts, the state is not "conducted on time" regardless of whether ballots are accepted in other congressional districts within that state.

An election that is postponed to, rescheduled to, conducted on, or otherwise held on a date other than the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026 in a state does not qualify as "conducted on time" in that state, regardless of the reason for the change of date and regardless of whether such change is lawful. This includes, without limitation, any change effected by federal legislation, executive order, presidential proclamation, federal agency directive, state law or proclamation, court order, or any other instrument. Ballots cast before the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026 through early voting do not, by themselves, satisfy this criterion in a state unless ballots are also lawfully accepted on the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026 in that state.

Special elections to fill vacancies, primary elections, and elections to non-voting delegate seats (including those representing the District of Columbia and U.S. territories) are not, by themselves, the "regularly scheduled biennial federal general election" referenced herein. The validity, fairness, certification status, or subsequent judicial treatment of any such election does not affect whether the election was "conducted on time" for purposes of this Contract; the test is whether election officials in the relevant state lawfully accepted ballots in the election on the federally prescribed Election Day for 2026.
markets.subtitle: Yes
markets.title: Will at least 50 states conduct 2026 U.S. House midterms on time?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if all elections have been decided and margins calculated.
markets.rules_primary: If Florida has the smallest margin of victory among all elections in the 2026 United States Senate elections as of Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Margin of victory is calculated as the absolute percentage point difference between first and second place finishers. For two-candidate races, this is winner's percentage minus runner-up's percentage. For multi-candidate races, only the gap between first and second counts. For ranked choice/instant runoff elections, the margin from the final round is used.

If official results aren't available by the deadline but at least 95% of expected vote is counted, preliminary results are used. In case of identical margins (tied to the hundredth of a percentage point), tied options split the payout equally. Postponed elections or those without sufficient results by the deadline resolve to No.
markets.title: Will Florida have the smallest margin of victory in 2026 United States Senate elections?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if all seats have been called and additional recounts/by-elections will not affect the market outcome.
markets.rules_primary: If Democrats win 2 seats in the 2026 U.S. House of Representatives elections in South Carolina, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A seat is considered "won" when a candidate affiliated with the specified party has been declared elected by the relevant electoral authority and either:
The time for legal challenges has expired
Challenges have been resolved
The member has taken their seat

Party affiliation is determined by the party under whose banner the candidate was elected, regardless of subsequent changes. The count is determined when the new legislature takes their seats, even if some seats remain vacant or challenged. If the election is postponed beyond one year from the original date or cancelled entirely, the market resolves to the last fair market price. Only seats actually contested and filled are counted in partial elections. By-elections after the main election are included only if seated simultaneously with the rest of the legislature.
markets.title: Will Democrats win exactly 2 seats in the 2026 U.S. House of Representatives elections in South Carolina?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the official vote count is certified.
markets.rules_primary: If the total vote count for all participants in Utah 03 House General Election is above 260000, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The vote count refers to the officially certified results from the relevant election authority. Provisional, absentee, early, mail-in, or electronic ballots are included only if reflected in the official certification. In preferential or ranked-choice systems, the contract resolves based on the vote count identified as the official result by the certifying authority. 

The contract resolves based on officially certified results regardless of ongoing appeals. Preliminary counts, exit polls, projections, or uncertified results do not qualify. If the election is postponed but held within one year of the originally scheduled date, the contract remains valid; if postponed beyond one year or canceled, all contracts resolve to No.
markets.title: Will the total vote count for all participants in Utah 03 House General Election be above 260000?

markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic Party wins the 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Utah's 1st District by 26 percentage points or more, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The margin of victory shall be calculated as follows based on the margin type.

For percentage points: the vote percentage received by the Democratic Party minus the vote percentage received by the candidate/party/option that finishes immediately behind the Democratic Party if the Democratic Party wins, or the candidate/party that finishes first if the Democratic Party loses.

Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound. No rounding shall be applied to the calculated margin. For example, for consecutive ranges of 5-6% and 6-7%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 5-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-7% range. If the Democratic Party runs under multiple parties or is listed multiple times, votes attributable to the same underlying natural the Democratic Party will be summed.

If the Democratic Party wins the election, the margin will be positive. If the Democratic Party loses the election, the margin will be negative. If the Democratic Party ties for first place, the margin shall be 0. For uncontested races where the Democratic Party is the only candidate, the margin shall be 100 percentage points or the total number of votes cast (for raw votes).

A seat is considered "won" when a candidate affiliated with the specified party has been declared elected by the relevant electoral authority and either:
The time for legal challenges has expired
Challenges have been resolved
The member has taken their seat

If the election is postponed beyond one year from the original date or cancelled entirely, the market resolves to the last fair market price. Only seats actually contested and filled are counted in partial elections. By-elections after the main election are included only if seated simultaneously with the rest of the legislature.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if certified election results are published.
markets.rules_primary: If the Republican Party wins the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Wyoming by 26 percentage points or more, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The margin of victory shall be calculated as follows based on the margin type.

For percentage points: the vote percentage received by the Republican Party minus the vote percentage received by the candidate/party/option that finishes immediately behind the Republican Party if the Republican Party wins, or the candidate/party that finishes first if the Republican Party loses.

Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound. No rounding shall be applied to the calculated margin. For example, for consecutive ranges of 5-6% and 6-7%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 5-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-7% range. If the Republican Party runs under multiple parties or is listed multiple times, votes attributable to the same underlying natural the Republican Party will be summed.

If the Republican Party wins the election, the margin will be positive. If the Republican Party loses the election, the margin will be negative. If the Republican Party ties for first place, the margin shall be 0. For uncontested races where the Republican Party is the only candidate, the margin shall be 100 percentage points or the total number of votes cast (for raw votes).
markets.title: Will the margin of victory for Republicans in the U.S. Senate election in Wyoming be at least 26 percentage points?

This includes:
Roll call votes
Recorded votes
Yea-and-nay votes
Electronic votes (in the House)
Division/standing votes

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Voice votes where individual member positions are not recorded
Unanimous consent agreements without a recorded vote
Votes in committee, unless the bill/motion specifically refers to a committee vote
Procedural determinations by the presiding officer
Deemed passage without an actual vote

For clarity:
A vote on cloture regarding the bill/motion, including cloture on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion, DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on the rule governing debate of the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion if the bill/motion specifically refers to that rule
A vote on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on final passage DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on an amendment to the bill/motion does NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion unless the bill/motion specifically refers to that amendment

markets.rules_secondary:
Margin of victory is calculated as the absolute percentage point difference between first and second place finishers. For two-candidate races, this is winner's percentage minus runner-up's percentage. For multi-candidate races, only the gap between first and second counts. For ranked choice/instant runoff elections, the margin from the final round is used.

If official results aren't available by the deadline but at least 95% of expected vote is counted, preliminary results are used. In case of identical margins (tied to the hundredth of a percentage point), tied options split the payout equally. Postponed elections or those without sufficient results by the deadline resolve to No.
